transform_notes: SAP's own key is MATNR (Material Number). Used as the staging key throughout this mapping (and must match whatever Product Catalog's MVKE rows use for the same physical item, since that sheet only has Item_ID as its join key, not Inventory Items' own Item_Code).

Company Code does not determine Plant or Valuation Area directly -- both need a real plant/valuation-area assignment from the target org structure, not just a Company Code lookup. Same class of gap as VKORG on Sales Orders.
BISMT exists specifically to carry a legacy material number forward without using it as the live MATNR -- a cleaner fit than the cross-reference-only pattern used for Employee_Code/Order_Number.
Lives on a separate language-dependent text table (MAKT), not on MARA itself. SPRAS (language) needs a constant, e.g. 'EN'.

Resolve via Inventory>Item Categories lookup (-> T134). Material Group (MATKL) is a related but distinct SAP concept (finer-grained reporting classification vs. MTART's structural material type) -- confirm which one this legacy category actually represents before finalizing; mapping it to the wrong one is a modeling error, not just an unresolved code.
Resolve via Inventory>Units of Measure lookup (-> T006).

Mapped by concept (a lower stock threshold), but 'safety stock' and 'minimum stock/order quantity' are not always the same thing in SAP configuration -- confirm the intended semantics with the business before load.
Same category of semantic confirmation as Min_Stock_Level.

Standard MARC-MINBE is per-PLANT. The separate legacy Inventory>Reorder Points table is per-(Item, Warehouse) with values that disagree with this one on essentially every overlapping row (verified: 93/93 mismatches) -- these are two different granularities of the same concept, not a duplicate to dedupe. If warehouses don't map 1:1 to plants in the target org structure, the per-warehouse table may need MRP areas or a custom table instead of a second MINBE value.

Also appears on Manufacturing>Product Catalog for the 15 items that have a sales-view row -- and disagrees on all 15 (verified), unlike Product_Name/Standard_Cost which are exact duplicates there. Because the values differ consistently rather than one side looking like noise (contrast with the Customers>Country investigation, where corroborating evidence pointed at one side being wrong), treat this as two plausibly distinct business concepts -- e.g. procurement replenishment lead time (here) vs. a customer-facing promised lead time (Product Catalog) -- and confirm with the business rather than assuming either is an error.
A boolean doesn't map directly to a profile code -- 'true' needs to resolve to an actual configured serial number profile in the target system, not just a flag flip.
Boolean maps reasonably well to SAP's 'X'/blank flag convention here.

Same ambiguity as Customers>Is_Active: SAP has no single 'active' flag on the material master, only block/deletion indicators at different levels (MARA-LVORM cross-plant vs. MARC-LVORM per-plant). All 100 rows are True in this data, so there's no evidence yet of which one 'inactive' would need to mean -- needs a business decision before mapping, same as Customers>Is_Active.
Every material master record stamps its own creation metadata automatically -- not loaded as source data.
Tracked via change documents (CDHDR/CDPOS) automatically -- not loaded as source data.
Legacy creator ID can be retained only as a migration audit/cross-reference attribute.
